summary: Runs an HTTP/WebSocket server inside TouchDesigner so web clients can connect, with request, WebSocket, binary data, startup, and shutdown handling delegated to callbacks.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Start or stop the web server

key_params.name: localaddress
key_params.note: IP address/interface to bind; blank listens on all interfaces

key_params.name: password
key_params.note: Certificate password; visually hidden but accessible by Python

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Required callback DAT for most server functionality

key_params.name: customext
key_params.note: Custom editor extension when extension mode uses a custom extension

common_gotchas: Most behavior goes through callbacks such as onHTTPRequest and WebSocket open/close/receive handlers.
Security is the project author's responsibility; authenticate requests and store secrets privately.
Leaving Local Address blank listens on every interface; use 127.0.0.1 for a local-only service.
Certificate passwords are only visually hidden and should be protected by putting the DAT in a private component when needed.
Secure TLS changes access from HTTP to HTTPS and requires valid key/certificate paths.
If exposing beyond localhost, account for firewall, CORS/application logic, and any authentication requirements.
key_concepts: Web Server DAT hosts HTTP and WebSocket endpoints inside TouchDesigner.
TouchDesigner 2025.33070+ can bind the listener to a selected interface through Local Address.
Request handling is callback-driven, including HTTP requests and WebSocket open/close/text/binary events.
TLS uses secure, private key, certificate, and certificate password parameters.
Security and authentication are the project author responsibility; sensitive certificate passwords should be protected in private components.
